_comment: Mutation testing for the TypeScript domains (src/builder/, src/release/, src/metrics/). The
Python side keeps mutmut over src/hooks/ (see pyproject.toml [tool.mutmut]); the two runs are
separate CI jobs named mutation-ts and mutation-py so they execute in PARALLEL rather than
serially — that parallelism is the reason the Python island is worth keeping at all.
The kill-rate gate itself is NOT enforced here. Stryker's own thresholds would report a second,
independently-configured number; instead src/release/checkMutationGate.mts reads the JSON report
and applies src/release/mutation-gate.json — the same file the Python gate reads. One threshold,
`mutate` covers src/builder/, src/release/ and src/metrics/, except each domain's own bin/. The
bin/ entry points are logic-free: they resolve a path, call one exported function and exit, so
every mutant in them is either equivalent or unkillable by a unit test. Excluding a logic-free
directory is honest; silencing individual mutants inside real logic is not, and the
`coverageAnalysis: all` rather than perTest — perTest mis-attributed coverage under the Vitest
runner and reported mutants as survived that the suite demonstrably kills.
